concepts.title: Reflection of Light by Spherical Mirrors
concepts.definition: A spherical mirror reflects light according to the laws of reflection, and the relationship between object distance, image distance and focal length is given by the mirror formula.
concepts.key_idea: For spherical mirrors the object distance u, image distance v and focal length f obey the mirror equation with sign convention applied.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics Ray Optics use the mirror formula to find image distance given object distance and focal length
calculate the position of the image formed by a concave mirror for a given object distance
determine focal length of a spherical mirror from object and image distances
find the nature and position of image formed by a convex mirror using mirror formula
apply sign convention to solve mirror equation for an object placed in front of a spherical mirror

solution_steps.action: apply sign convention to object distance and focal length
solution_steps.explain: take object distance u as negative for real objects and assign focal length f negative for concave and positive for convex mirrors

solution_steps.action: substitute values into the mirror formula
solution_steps.explain: use 1/v + 1/u = 1/f and solve for the image distance v

solution_steps.action: interpret the sign of v to determine image nature
solution_steps.explain: a positive v gives a virtual erect image behind the mirror while a negative v gives a real inverted image in front of the mirror
solution_steps.compute: image_nature = virtual if v > 0 else real

worked_examples.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the image distance.
worked_examples.answer: v = -30 cm (real, inverted, same size image)

worked_examples.question: An object is placed 10 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the image distance.

exercises.question: An object is placed 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Find the position and nature of the image.
A convex mirror of focal length 20 cm forms an image 10 cm behind the mirror. Find the object distance.

concepts.title: Refraction of Light and Snell Law
concepts.definition: When light travels from one transparent medium to another it bends at the interface, and the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant called the refractive index.
concepts.key_idea: Snell law relates the angles of incidence and refraction to the refractive indices of the two media at an optical interface.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics Ray Optics apply Snell law to find angle of refraction given angle of incidence
calculate the refractive index of a medium using Snell law
determine the angle of refraction when light passes from air into glass
find the speed of light in a medium given its refractive index
verify Snell law for a ray crossing the boundary between two transparent media

solution_steps.action: identify refractive indices of the two media
solution_steps.explain: n1 is the refractive index of the incident medium and n2 is the refractive index of the refracting medium

solution_steps.action: apply Snell law to relate angles
solution_steps.explain: use n1 * sin(i) = n2 * sin(r) and solve for the unknown angle

solution_steps.action: compute the refraction angle and verify it is physically valid
solution_steps.explain: take the inverse sine of sin(r); if sin(r) exceeds 1 total internal reflection occurs instead of refraction

worked_examples.question: A ray of light travelling in air is incident on a glass surface at 45 degrees. If the refractive index of glass is 1.5, find the angle of refraction.
The speed of light in a medium is 2 x 10^8 m/s. Find the refractive index of the medium.

exercises.question: Light travels from water (n = 1.33) into air (n = 1) at an angle of incidence of 30 degrees. Find the angle of refraction.
The refractive index of diamond is 2.42. Find the speed of light in diamond.

concepts.title: Total Internal Reflection
concepts.definition: When light travels from a denser to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, the ray is completely reflected back into the denser medium.
concepts.formula: sin(ic) = n2 / n1 where n1 > n2
concepts.key_idea: Total internal reflection occurs only when light goes from a denser to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics Ray Optics calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection
determine whether a ray undergoes total internal reflection at a given angle of incidence
find the critical angle for light passing from glass to air
explain the condition for total internal reflection in optical fibres
verify that the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle for total internal reflection

solution_steps.action: compute the critical angle from refractive indices
solution_steps.explain: the critical angle is given by sin(ic) = n2 / n1 where n1 is the denser medium and n2 is the rarer medium

solution_steps.action: compare the angle of incidence with the critical angle
solution_steps.explain: total internal reflection occurs only when the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle

solution_steps.action: verify the direction of light travel
solution_steps.explain: confirm that light is travelling from the denser medium to the rarer medium, otherwise total internal reflection cannot occur

worked_examples.question: The refractive index of glass is 1.5. Find the critical angle for total internal reflection when light travels from glass to air.
A ray of light travelling in water (n = 1.33) is incident on the water-air interface at 50 degrees. Does total internal reflection occur?
worked_examples.solution: sin(ic) = 1/1.33 = 0.752, ic = 48.8 deg. Since 50 deg > 48.8 deg, total internal reflection occurs.

exercises.question: Find the critical angle for a medium of refractive index 1.6 in contact with air.
Light travels from glass (n = 1.5) to water (n = 1.33) at an angle of 70 degrees. Determine whether total internal reflection takes place.

concepts.title: Refraction at Spherical Surfaces
concepts.definition: When light refracts at a spherical surface separating two media, the object distance, image distance and radii of curvature are related by the refraction formula at a single spherical surface.
concepts.key_idea: Refraction at a spherical surface depends on the refractive indices of the two media, the radius of curvature of the surface and the object and image distances.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics Ray Optics find image distance for refraction at a spherical surface
calculate the position of the image formed by refraction at a convex spherical surface
determine the radius of curvature of a spherical refracting surface
apply the refraction formula at a single spherical surface separating two media
verify the image position for a ray refracting through a spherical interface

solution_steps.action: assign refractive indices and radius of curvature with sign convention
solution_steps.explain: n1 is the object side medium and n2 is the image side medium; R is positive if the surface is convex towards the rarer medium
solution_steps.compute: n1 = object_medium; n2 = image_medium; R = signed_radius

solution_steps.action: substitute into the refraction formula
solution_steps.explain: use (n2/v) - (n1/u) = (n2 - n1)/R and solve for the image distance v

solution_steps.action: interpret the sign of v for image nature
solution_steps.explain: a positive v indicates a real image on the image side while a negative v indicates a virtual image on the object side
solution_steps.compute: image_nature = real if v > 0 else virtual

worked_examples.question: An object is placed at 25 cm from a convex spherical surface of radius 10 cm separating air (n1 = 1) from glass (n2 = 1.5). Find the image distance.
A small object is placed in air at 30 cm from a concave spherical surface of radius 5 cm separating air from glass (n = 1.5). Find the image distance.
worked_examples.answer: v = -11.25 cm (virtual image on object side)

exercises.question: An object is placed 40 cm from a convex spherical surface of radius 20 cm separating air (n = 1) from water (n = 1.33). Find the image distance.
A point object is placed in glass (n = 1.5) at 15 cm from a plane surface separating glass from air. Find the apparent depth of the object.

concepts.title: Lens Maker Formula
concepts.definition: The lens maker formula relates the focal length of a thin lens to its refractive index and the radii of curvature of its two surfaces.
concepts.key_idea: The focal length of a lens depends on the refractive index of the lens material and the radii of curvature of its two surfaces with proper sign convention.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics Ray Optics use the lens maker formula to find the focal length of a lens
calculate the focal length of a biconvex lens given its radii of curvature and refractive index
determine the refractive index of a lens material from its focal length and radii
apply the lens maker formula to a plano-convex lens
verify the focal length of a thin lens using the lens maker equation

solution_steps.action: assign radii of curvature with sign convention
solution_steps.explain: R1 is positive for a convex first surface and R2 is negative for a convex second surface; both signs follow the direction of incident light

solution_steps.action: substitute into the lens maker formula
solution_steps.explain: use 1/f = (n - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2) and compute the reciprocal of the focal length

solution_steps.action: compute the focal length and its nature
solution_steps.explain: take the reciprocal of inv_f; a positive f indicates a converging lens and a negative f indicates a diverging lens

worked_examples.question: A biconvex lens has radii of curvature 20 cm and 30 cm and refractive index 1.5. Find its focal length.
A plano-convex lens has a curved surface of radius 10 cm and refractive index 1.5. Find its focal length.

exercises.question: A biconcave lens has radii of curvature 25 cm and 25 cm and refractive index 1.5. Find its focal length.
A thin lens of refractive index 1.6 has focal length 20 cm. If R1 = 30 cm, find R2.

concepts.title: Combination of Thin Lenses in Contact
concepts.definition: When several thin lenses are placed in contact, the equivalent focal length is obtained by adding the reciprocals of the individual focal lengths.
concepts.key_idea: The power of a combination of thin lenses in contact is the algebraic sum of the powers of the individual lenses.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics Ray Optics find the equivalent focal length of two thin lenses in contact
calculate the equivalent power of a combination of lenses
determine the focal length of a lens combination of a converging and a diverging lens
apply the lens combination formula to three thin lenses in contact
verify the equivalent focal length of lenses placed together

solution_steps.action: list the focal lengths of all lenses with sign convention
solution_steps.explain: converging lenses have positive focal lengths and diverging lenses have negative focal lengths

solution_steps.action: sum the reciprocals of the focal lengths
solution_steps.explain: the reciprocal of the equivalent focal length equals the sum of the reciprocals of individual focal lengths
solution_steps.compute: inv_F = sum(1/f for f in f_list)

solution_steps.action: compute the equivalent focal length and power
solution_steps.explain: take the reciprocal of inv_F to get F; the equivalent power is P = 1/F in metres inverse

worked_examples.question: Two thin lenses of focal lengths 20 cm and -30 cm are placed in contact. Find the equivalent focal length and power.
Three thin lenses of focal lengths 30 cm, 30 cm and -15 cm are in contact. Find the equivalent focal length.
worked_examples.answer: F = infinity (acts like a plane glass plate)

exercises.question: Two lenses of focal lengths 15 cm and 25 cm are placed in contact. Find the equivalent focal length.
A converging lens of focal length 20 cm is in contact with a diverging lens of focal length 20 cm. Find the power of the combination.

concepts.title: Magnification by Lens and Mirror
concepts.definition: Linear magnification produced by a lens or mirror is the ratio of the image height to the object height, and is also equal to the ratio of image distance to object distance.
concepts.formula: m = h2/h1 = v/u (for lens); m = -v/u (for mirror)
concepts.key_idea: Magnification relates the size and orientation of the image to the object through the image and object distances.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics Ray Optics calculate the magnification produced by a lens
find the magnification of an image formed by a concave mirror
determine the size of the image given the object size and magnification
compute the magnification of a convex mirror for a given object distance
verify whether the image is erect or inverted using the sign of magnification

solution_steps.action: identify object distance and image distance with sign convention
solution_steps.explain: use the mirror or lens formula to find v and keep the signed values of u and v

solution_steps.action: apply the magnification formula
solution_steps.explain: for a mirror use m = -v/u and for a lens use m = v/u
solution_steps.compute: m = -v/u for mirror; m = v/u for lens

solution_steps.action: compute image height and interpret the sign of m
solution_steps.explain: a positive m gives an erect virtual image while a negative m gives an inverted real image; image height h2 = m * h1

worked_examples.question: An object 2 cm tall is placed 15 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Find the magnification and image size.
worked_examples.answer: m = -2, image height = 4 cm (real, inverted, enlarged)

worked_examples.question: An object 3 cm tall is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Find the magnification and image size.
worked_examples.answer: m = -2, image height = 6 cm (real, inverted, enlarged)

exercises.question: An object 5 cm tall is placed 25 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the magnification and image height.
A convex lens of focal length 10 cm forms an image at 30 cm on the other side. Find the magnification if the object is 2 cm tall.

concepts.title: Power of a Lens
concepts.definition: The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length expressed in metres, and it measures the degree of convergence or divergence produced by the lens.
concepts.key_idea: A converging lens has positive power and a diverging lens has negative power; the SI unit of power is the dioptre.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics Ray Optics calculate the power of a lens given its focal length
find the focal length of a lens from its power in dioptres
determine the power of a combination of two lenses in contact
compute the power of a converging lens of focal length 25 cm
verify the sign of power for a diverging lens

solution_steps.action: convert focal length to metres with sign convention
solution_steps.explain: converging lens has positive f and diverging lens has negative f; convert cm to m by dividing by 100

solution_steps.action: compute the power as reciprocal of focal length in metres
solution_steps.explain: power in dioptres equals 1 divided by focal length in metres

solution_steps.action: interpret the sign of power
solution_steps.explain: a positive power indicates a converging lens and a negative power indicates a diverging lens
solution_steps.compute: lens_type = converging if P > 0 else diverging

worked_examples.question: Find the power of a converging lens of focal length 25 cm.
A diverging lens has focal length 50 cm. Find its power.

exercises.question: Find the power of a lens of focal length -40 cm.
The power of a lens is +2.5 D. Find its focal length in cm.

concepts.title: Prism Formula and Dispersion
concepts.definition: When light passes through a prism it bends towards the base, and the angle of deviation depends on the angle of incidence, the prism angle and the refractive index of the prism material.
concepts.formula: delta = (i + e) - A; n = sin((A + delta_min)/2) / sin(A/2)
concepts.key_idea: The minimum deviation through a prism occurs when the ray passes symmetrically and the refractive index is related to the prism angle and minimum deviation.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics Ray Optics calculate the angle of deviation through a prism
find the refractive index of a prism using the minimum deviation formula
determine the minimum angle of deviation for a given prism angle and refractive index
compute the refractive index of a prism given the angle of minimum deviation
verify the condition for minimum deviation in a prism

solution_steps.action: identify the prism angle and angle of minimum deviation
solution_steps.explain: the prism angle A is the angle between the two refracting surfaces and delta_min is the minimum angle of deviation

solution_steps.action: apply the prism formula for refractive index
solution_steps.explain: use n = sin((A + delta_min)/2) / sin(A/2) to compute the refractive index of the prism material

solution_steps.action: verify the result is physically consistent
solution_steps.explain: the refractive index must be greater than 1 for a real prism and the angles must be in degrees converted to radians for computation

worked_examples.question: A prism has an angle of 60 degrees and produces a minimum deviation of 30 degrees. Find the refractive index of the prism.
The refractive index of a prism of angle 60 degrees is 1.5. Find the angle of minimum deviation.
worked_examples.solution: n = 1.5, A = 60 deg. 1.5 = sin((60 + delta_min)/2) / sin(30) = sin((60 + delta_min)/2) / 0.5. sin((60 + delta_min)/2) = 0.75. (60 + delta_min)/2 = 48.6 deg. 60 + delta_min = 97.2 deg. delta_min = 37.2 deg.

exercises.question: A prism of angle 60 degrees has a refractive index of 1.33. Find the angle of minimum deviation.
A prism produces a minimum deviation of 40 degrees for an angle of 60 degrees. Find the refractive index.

concepts.title: Optical Instruments: Microscope and Telescope
concepts.definition: Optical instruments use combinations of lenses to produce magnified images; a compound microscope uses an objective and an eyepiece to view tiny objects while a telescope is used to view distant objects.
concepts.key_idea: The magnifying power of a microscope depends on the objective and eyepiece focal lengths and the near point, while a telescope magnifying power is the ratio of the objective focal length to the eyepiece focal length.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics Ray Optics calculate the magnifying power of a compound microscope
find the magnifying power of an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment
determine the magnification of a telescope given the focal lengths of objective and eyepiece
compute the magnifying power of a microscope for the final image at the near point
verify the magnifying power of an optical instrument using its lens parameters

solution_steps.action: identify the focal lengths of the objective and eyepiece
solution_steps.explain: for a microscope f_o and f_e are the focal lengths of the objective and eyepiece and D is the least distance of distinct vision
solution_steps.compute: f_o = objective_f; f_e = eyepiece_f; D = 25 cm

solution_steps.action: apply the magnifying power formula for the instrument
solution_steps.explain: for a microscope use M = (v_o/u_o)(1 + D/f_e) and for a telescope in normal adjustment use M = f_o/f_e
solution_steps.compute: M = f_o / f_e for telescope; M = (v_o/u_o) * (1 + D/f_e) for microscope

solution_steps.action: compute the magnifying power and interpret the result
solution_steps.explain: a larger magnifying power means a greater angular size of the final image seen by the eye

worked_examples.question: A compound microscope has an objective of focal length 1 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 5 cm. The final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision D = 25 cm. If the object is placed 1.1 cm from the objective, find the magnifying power.
An astronomical telescope has an objective of focal length 100 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 5 cm. Find the magnifying power in normal adjustment.

exercises.question: A telescope has an objective of focal length 80 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 4 cm. Find its magnifying power in normal adjustment.

A compound microscope has an objective of focal length 2 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 10 cm. The final image is formed at 25 cm and the object is placed at 2.2 cm from the objective. Find the magnifying power.
